f: Ashutosh Kumar Thakur is a Bengaluru-based writer, literary critic, translator and festival curator. An alumnus of Banaras Hindu University, he serves as Co-Director and Curator of the Banaras Literature Festival. He writes in English and Hindi on literature, culture and politics for leading publications, including The Hindu Literary Review, The Indian Express, Outlook, Scroll and The Wire. He is currently translating selected Maithili short stories by Harimohan Jha and Vyomesh Shukla’s Aag Aur Paani into English, while championing Indian-language literature through translation, criticism and literary programming.

b: Avni Doshi is the author of Burnt Sugar , first published in India as Girl in White Cotton . The novel won the 2021 Sushila Devi Award and was longlisted for the 2019 Tata First Novel Prize. It was shortlisted for the…
f: Avni Doshi is the author of Burnt Sugar , first published in India as Girl in White Cotton . The novel won the 2021 Sushila Devi Award and was longlisted for the 2019 Tata First Novel Prize. It was shortlisted for the 2020 Booker Prize and named a Book of the Year by The Guardian , The Economist , The Spectator and NPR. It was also longlisted for the Women’s Prize, named one of The New York Times Book Review ’s 100 Notable Books and shortlisted for the PEN/Hemingway Award. Her work has been translated into twenty-six languages. The First House is her second book.

f: Jeyamohan is one of India's most acclaimed contemporary writers, with nearly 300 books in Tamil and Malayalam spanning fiction, literary criticism, travel writing, and philosophy. His 24-volume Venmurasu , a modern retelling of the Mahabharata , is a landmark of Indian literature. His works have been published in English in India, the United States, and the United Kingdom. He is the founder of the Vishnupuram Literary Circle, Tamil Wiki, and Nithya Vanam, a centre for philosophical learning.

f: Bertil Lintner left Sweden for Asia in 1975 and has worked for the Far Eastern Economic Review , Scandinavian dailies, and Asia Times . b: DhrubaJyoti Borah (D.J.B.) is one of the foremost voices in contemporary Assamese literature. Equally accomplished in fiction and non-fiction, he has authored more than thirty novels. His acclaimed works include the…
f: DhrubaJyoti Borah (D.J.B.) is one of the foremost voices in contemporary Assamese literature. Equally accomplished in fiction and non-fiction, he has authored more than thirty novels. His notable non-fiction includes Peasant–Rebel–Soldier–King , a study of the Moamoria uprising, alongside influential works on the Assamese language and questions of nationhood and self-determination.

b: Gautam Choubey is a translator, columnist, and novelist whose work spans Hindi, Bhojpuri, and English literature. He has translated Suryakant Tripathi ‘Nirala’ and André Béteille, and co-translated the Hindi bestseller…

f: Steve Brusatte is a palaeontologist and professor at the University of Edinburgh, Scotland. An expert on the anatomy and evolution of dinosaurs, birds, and mammals, he has described more than 20 new extinct species from fossils. He is the author of the internationally bestselling books The Rise and Fall of the Dinosaurs and The Story of Birds . Brusatte also serves as the palaeontology consultant for the Jurassic World film franchise and the BBC's Walking With Dinosaurs .

bk.t: The Rise and Fall of the Dinosaurs
Rise and Reign of the Mammals

f: Subi Taba is an award-winning author and civil servant from Arunachal Pradesh. Her debut fiction, Tales from the Dawn-Lit Mountains , won the Ramnath Goenka Sahithya Samman 2025, AutHer Award for Best Debut and Legacy of Literature Editor’s Choice Award 2025. A recipient of the New Asian Short Story Prize, she is also a South Asia Speaks fellow.

b: Sudeep Chakravarti is a chronicler, historian, columnist, policy analyst, and educator whose work explores history, ethnography, culture, conflict and conflict resolution, and transboundary relations across South Asia…
f: Sudeep Chakravarti is a chronicler, historian, columnist, policy analyst, and educator whose work explores history, ethnography, culture, conflict and conflict resolution, and transboundary relations across South Asia and the Indian Ocean region. His books, which have received several honours, include The Bengalis, Plassey, Red Sun, The Eastern Gate, Highway 39 , and Fallen City . His latest book, Humayun: The Life, Death, and Afterlife of an Emperor , explores the life and legacy of the Mughal emperor.

bk.t: The Bengalis, Plassey, Red Sun, The Eastern Gate, Highway 39
Humayun: The Life, Death, and Afterlife of an Emperor

b: Dr. Suraj Yengde is the author of Caste: A Global Story , published internationally by Oxford University Press, C. Hurst & Co., and Allen Lane. Named History Today’s Best Book of the Year 2025, it examines caste as a…
f: Dr. Suraj Yengde is the author of Caste: A Global Story , published internationally by Oxford University Press, C. Hurst & Co., and Allen Lane. Named History Today’s Best Book of the Year 2025, it examines caste as a global phenomenon. Yengde was a consultant and co-producer on Ava DuVernay’s Origin . He is Founding Director and Principal Investigator of the Global Caste Lab at the University of Pennsylvania, where he teaches. His second doctorate from the University of Oxford traced the global histories of caste and race through Dalit and Black intellectual thought.

b: Sven Beckert is Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University in the United States. His latest book, Capitalism: A Global History , has been published by Penguin. His previous book, Empire of Cotton , won the…
f: Sven Beckert is Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University in the United States. His latest book, Capitalism: A Global History , has been published by Penguin. His previous book, Empire of Cotton , won the Bancroft Prize, was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize and was named one of the ten best books of the year by The New York Times . Beckert is a Guggenheim Fellow and an elected member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

b: Tabeenah Anjum is an award-winning journalist and photographer with over 15 years of experience covering politics, gender, human rights, migration and marginalised communities in Rajasthan and neighbouring states. Her…
f: Tabeenah Anjum is an award-winning journalist and photographer with over 15 years of experience covering politics, gender, human rights, migration and marginalised communities in Rajasthan and neighbouring states. Her reportage appears in Outlook , The Quint , Article 14 , Times of India Plus and BBC. Her debut book, From Dynasties to Democracy: Politics, Caste and Power Struggles in Rajasthan , is published by Pan Macmillan. A PhD in Journalism and Mass Communication, she teaches in India and abroad. Her awards include the National Award in Photography (2015) and the Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II Award (2017).

bk.t: From Dynasties to Democracy: Politics, Caste and Power Struggles in Rajasthan

f: Tabish Khair ’s new novel is Drown All the Refugees ; in 2024, his study, Literature Against Fundamentalism, was published. His other novels and books have been translated into various languages and shortlisted for national and international awards. He is also the winner of the All India Poetry Prize.

bk.t: How To Fight Islamist Terror From The Missionary Position

b: Tahmima Anam ’s debut novel, A Golden Age , won the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize for Best First Book and was shortlisted for the Guardian First Book Award. Her second novel, The Good Muslim , was shortlisted for the 2013…
f: Tahmima Anam ’s debut novel, A Golden Age , won the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize for Best First Book and was shortlisted for the Guardian First Book Award. Her second novel, The Good Muslim , was shortlisted for the 2013 DSC Prize for South Asian Literature. Her most recent novels include The Startup Wife (2021) and Uprising (2026). Her writing has appeared in The Guardian , the Financial Times and Freeman’s . She is a Contributing Opinion Writer for The New York Times and was named one of Granta’s Best of Young British Novelists in 2013.

f: Tavleen Singh is the author of six books on Indian politics. Her latest book, The Actor , is her debut novel. She writes two columns a week, one in Hindi for Jansatta and the other in English for The Indian Express .

f: Dr. Thangjam Hindustani Devi is a linguist and author whose work spans poetry, culture, and folklore. After a seventeen-year career at Google, she turned to writing, co-authoring Feathers, Fools and Farts: Manipuri Folktales Retold (Puffin), which brings the rich tradition of Manipuri oral narratives to a new generation. Her debut poetry collection, Whispering Pines , explores themes of memory, emotional landscapes, and loss.

bk.t: Feathers, Fools and Farts: Manipuri Folktales Retold
Girls Are Coming out of the Woods

b: Vali Nasr is the Majid Khadduri Professor of International Affairs and Middle East Studies and Senior Non-Resident Advisor at CSIS. A leading scholar of the Middle East, he is the author of several influential books,…
f: Vali Nasr is the Majid Khadduri Professor of International Affairs and Middle East Studies and Senior Non-Resident Advisor at CSIS. A leading scholar of the Middle East, he is the author of several influential books, most recently Iran’s Grand Strategy: A Political History . He served as the Henry Alfred Kissinger Distinguished Scholar at the Library of Congress for 2024–25, where he pursued research on the history and politics of Iran and the broader Middle East.

bk.t: Iran’s Grand Strategy: A Political History

b: Vasudhendra is an Indian author who writes in Kannada. His 16 books have been translated into several Indian languages, as well as English and Spanish. He has run the Kannada publishing house Chanda Pustaka for 21…
f: Vasudhendra is an Indian author who writes in Kannada. His 16 books have been translated into several Indian languages, as well as English and Spanish. He has run the Kannada publishing house Chanda Pustaka for 21 years, supporting emerging Kannada writers. He is the first openly gay author in Kannada. An avid hiker, he has trekked across the Western Ghats, Mount Kilimanjaro, Kailash-Mansarovar and the Himalayas. His other interests include world cinema, the Mahabharata and Indian classical music.

b: Veena Karamchandani is a distinguished Hindi and Sindhi writer with nearly 35 years of literary experience. She is the author of three books and a recipient of the Rajasthan Sindhi Academy State-Level Award. Her writing…
f: Veena Karamchandani is a distinguished Hindi and Sindhi writer with nearly 35 years of literary experience. She is the author of three books and a recipient of the Rajasthan Sindhi Academy State-Level Award. Her writing has appeared in leading literary journals, and she has represented Sindhi literature at prominent national forums, including the Sahitya Akademi’s Festival of Letters, national literary symposiums and All India Radio’s All-Languages Poets’ Conferences. Her work reflects a sustained engagement with the literary traditions and cultural heritage of Sindhi and Hindi.

b: Vighnesh Hampapura is a translator, writer and musician. His translations of Vivek Shanbhag’s On One Side, The Sea , Vasudhendra’s short stories and Vatsyayana’s Kamasutra are at various stages of publication. In 2025,…
f: Vighnesh Hampapura is a translator, writer and musician. His translations of Vivek Shanbhag’s On One Side, The Sea , Vasudhendra’s short stories and Vatsyayana’s Kamasutra are at various stages of publication. In 2025, he received a PEN Presents x SALT shortlist grant for his translation work. His fiction and criticism have appeared in Scroll , Literary Activism , L’Indiscreto , Bhanuprabha , Bridge of Stories and The Women’s Studies Journal . He practises Karnatik music and has performed themed recitals, including Notes on Love , in Delhi, Bengaluru, Mysuru and Oxford.

b: Vikas Swarup is a former diplomat, television host and bestselling author. His debut novel, Q&A , was adapted into the Oscar-winning film Slumdog Millionaire . His other novels include Six Suspects , adapted into the…
f: Vikas Swarup is a former diplomat, television host and bestselling author. His debut novel, Q&A , was adapted into the Oscar-winning film Slumdog Millionaire . His other novels include Six Suspects , adapted into the television series The Great Indian Murder , The Accidental Apprentice and The Girl with the Seven Lives . His books have been translated into 47 languages, and he has received four honorary doctorates.

bk.t: The Girl with the Seven Lives

b: Vineet Nayar is the former CEO of HCL Technologies and the author of the global bestseller Employees First, Customer Second , one of the most influential management books of the last two decades. At HCLT, he led a…
f: Vineet Nayar is the former CEO of HCL Technologies and the author of the global bestseller Employees First, Customer Second , one of the most influential management books of the last two decades. At HCLT, he led a celebrated transformation of the IT industry by placing human potential at the heart of business performance. Today, as Founder-Chairman of Sampark Foundation, he works to transform learning outcomes for millions of children across rural India through technology designed to amplify human potential, not replace it.

bk.t: Zuerst der Mitarbeiter, Dann der Kunde Stellen Siedas Konventionelle Management Auf Den Kopf
